resources.string: How the glomerular filtration barrier works
A qualitative close-up of one glomerular capillary wall in a healthy kidney. Structures and particles are not to scale. The urinary side contains newly formed filtrate, not final urine.
At the start of a nephron, blood flows through a tuft of capillaries called the glomerulus. The close-up shows one wall between capillary blood and the urinary space of Bowman\'s capsule.
Small openings called fenestrae pass through thin regions of the cells lining the capillary. They are on the blood side of the barrier and do not open directly into the urinary space.
A continuous basement membrane lies directly between the capillary lining and the podocyte foot processes. It is a shared layer of the same capillary wall.
Foot processes from neighboring podocytes interleave on the urinary side of the basement membrane. Thin slit diaphragms span the narrow gaps between adjacent processes.

Across all three layers, some water and small dissolved solutes enter the urinary space as filtrate. Blood cells and most large proteins stay in the bloodstream. This is the combined result of the whole barrier.
